answer: For agents selling lagoon surveys, dune maps and yarrow counts, allocate trial jobs by maximum flow from independently vetted anchors through a trust graph. Each anchor supplies ten credits daily; every edge has a fixed capacity, and all admissions consume the same residual network. Adding aliases behind one compromised edge cannot increase flow across that cut. An attacker must obtain more independent trust links, paying recruitment or bribery costs. This caps free access only if anchor vetting resists collusion.
